Borrowing from an Oghur language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Compare Chuvash сысна (sysna, “pig”), Eastern Mari сӧсна (sösna, “pig”). Dialectal gyisznó retains an older form of the word.

From an Oghur language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries, from Proto-Turkic *erk (“strength, might, will, power”).

Borrowing from an Oghur language, before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Compare Proto-Common Turkic *yula (“torch”).

parole.significato: fruit (typically sweet or sour edible part of a plant)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Hungarian gyimilcs, borrowed from an Oghur language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), from Proto-Turkic *yẹ̄miĺč (“fruit”). Cognates include Bashkir емеш (yemeş), Chuvash ҫимӗҫ (śimĕś), Turkish yemiş.

parole.significato: ring, finger ring (object designed to be worn on a finger)
parole.testo: Borrowed from an Oghur language, from Proto-Turkic *yüŕük (“ring”). Compare Chuvash ҫӗрӗ (śĕrĕ), Turkish yüzük (“ring”).

parole.significato: polecat (a weasel-like animal of the genus Mustela)
parole.testo: An Oghur borrowing, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *küŕen (“ferret, weasel”). See Bashkir көҙән (köðän) for more.
From an Oghur language, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yẹr. Compare Chuvash ҫӗр (śĕr) and Turkish yer.
Borrowed from an Oghur source — compare Chuvash ҫӳҫ (śüś, “hair; filament”), from Proto-Turkic *sač (“hair”).

parole.significato: mud (a mixture of water and soil or fine grained sediment)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Oghur *šār (compare Chuvash шур (šur, “swamp”)), from Proto-Turkic *siāŕ (“marsh, dirt”). Compare also Bashkir һаҙ (hað, “swamp, marsh”), Kazakh саз (saz, “mud”).

Borrowing from an Oghur language, before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), from Proto-Turkic *tāŕ (“bald”). Cognates include Turkish dazlak (“bald”), Karakhanid تازْ (tāz, “bald”), and Middle Mongol ᠲᠠᠷᠠᠰᠤᠨ (tarasun, “bald”), the
From an Oghur language, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *teŋiŕ. Cognates include Turkish deniz, Kazakh теңіз (teŋiz), and Chuvash тинӗс (tinĕs).

parole.significato: steer (the castrated male of cattle, a young bullock)
parole.testo: From Oghur, from Proto-Turkic *tāna, possibly of Iranian origin, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dʰa(H)inúš. Compare Chuvash тына (tyna, “heifer”), Turkish dana (“calf, steer”), Sanskrit धेनु (dhenu, “(milk) cow”).

Borrowing from an Oghur language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Compare Chuvash тӗкӗр (tĕk̬ĕr, “mirror”), Western Mari тӹгӹр (tÿgÿr, “mirror”).

parole.significato: ox (a castrated bull over 4 years old regardless of age at castration)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Oghur, from Proto-Turkic *öküŕ (“ox”). Compare Chuvash вӑкӑр (văk̬ăr), Mongolian үхэр (üxer); cf. also Oghuz Turkish öküz.
